newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo tea prices fall in latest auction.
newsitem.headline: Colombo tea prices fall in latest auction.

text.p: Tea prices at the Colombo auction fell because most buyers were away on holiday, brokers said on Wednesday.
"Prices fell mainly because of the holiday period," said a broker. "Many businesses are closed, particularly in the West."
Buyers were hesitant to place orders because they can't ship any goods out until after the Christmas holidays, the broker added.
The anticipated gross sale average for the 5.9 million kg on offer fell to 102 rupees ($1.80) per kg from 105.51 rupees last week, brokers Forbes & Walker said.
Iraq, once the biggest buyer of Ceylon tea, was still not back in the Colombo auction because prices were too high, brokers and exporters said.
"The Colombo auction average price is the highest now mainly because of CIS demand," a broker said. "Traditional buyers find it difficult to get quantities because of high prices."
Colombo tea prices soared to record highs in recent months because of buying by the CIS.
The next auction is on January 2 when 3.8 million kg will be on offer. ($=56.46 rupees)
